title: The agent serves no JMAP WebSocket, so a client can send a call signal but never receive one
description:
Found 2026-11-23 while working out what a Parlor-shaped demo client for
mimid would need. This is the one thing that stops a call connecting.

THE GAP. VTCCall/signal works: a client sends a session description or
candidate and the agent puts it in the call room's messages
(commit b29cd913). The other direction does not exist.
draft-atwood-jmap-vtc-00 specifies VTCCallSignal as an EPHEMERAL
WEBSOCKET EVENT, and the agent's loopback endpoint serves no JMAP
WebSocket. What it serves is GET /jmap/eventsource, which carries
RFC 8620 §7.3 StateChange objects: "these types changed, re-fetch". A
signal is not a state change and has no record to re-fetch -- that is
decision mimid-1wgh.117's point, that signalling is not content.

So mimid's own VtcBackend::deliver_event drops, and its documentation
says why. A demo client would offer a call, send its SDP, and wait
forever.

HOW PARLOR SOLVES IT, which is the model to follow: its client opens a
WebSocket to each relay, sends REQ with filters, and the relay pushes
EVENT frames (web/nostr.js subscribe/handleMessage). It re-sends every
subscription on reconnect (resubscribeAll), bounds the queue it holds
while disconnected (MAX_QUEUE_SIZE 100), and bounds reconnection
(MAX_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS 5, backoff capped at 60s). A bidirectional
socket is what a calling client holds anyway.

THE OPTIONS, in the order I would rank them:

1. A JMAP WEBSOCKET ON THE AGENT. crate-jmap has crate-jmap-websocket
   already, and jmap-vtc-types already defines
   JMAP_VTC_WEBSOCKET_URI. This is what the draft assumes, it makes the
   demo client ordinary rather than special, and the agent's endpoint
   already authenticates a bearer credential it could reuse.
2. CARRY SIGNALS OVER THE EXISTING EVENTSOURCE as an event that is not
   a StateChange. Cheapest: the stream exists and is authenticated. But
   it extends RFC 8620's event stream with our own event type, which
   belongs in the draft rather than done quietly.
3. POLL. Needs signals stored and fetchable, which contradicts their
   being ephemeral, and would put SDP in the store for no one's benefit.
   Not recommended.

NEEDS MARK: which of the three. Everything else for a keyed 1:1 call is
built.
notes:
DECIDED: mimid-1wgh.122, a JMAP WebSocket on the agent. The EventSource option was rejected because a non-StateChange event in RFC 8620's stream is a change to the stream that would need writing into the draft; polling because it contradicts signals being ephemeral.
THE RECORD IS BEAD mimid-1wgh.100, not mimid-1wgh.122: the WebSocket's placement was settled 2026-11-22 and .100 carries the reasoning, including why RFC 8887 must not replace the live stream. .100's open question applies here: the Session advertises both chat:websocket and vtc:websocket, and neither draft says what a server does when a client uses one draft's subscribe mechanism and not the other's.
